cands.name: Greg Steube
cands.bio: Republican U.S. Representative since 2019 (Ways and Means Committee). Army JAG captain (2004-2008, Iraq deployment); UF Law J.D. Florida House 2010-2016 and Florida Senate (District 23) 2016-2018. Son of former Manatee County Sheriff Brad Steube.
cands.local_ties: Born in Bradenton; lives in Sarasota per Wikipedia.

record.text: Committees: Ways and Means (Oversight, Social Security and Trade subcommittees) and the Select Subcommittee on the Weaponization of the Federal Government (118th Congress).
Sponsor of the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act (H.R. 734 in 2023; H.R. 28 in 2025, which passed the House 218-206 and failed a Senate cloture vote 51-45).

money_notes.text: Endorsed by AIPAC and the Associated Builders and Contractors Florida Gulf Coast Chapter (per Wikipedia's 2026 election page).

controversies.text: Feb. 2021: skipped House votes via proxy while attending CPAC; a watchdog group filed an ethics complaint; Wikipedia notes no evidence the Ethics Committee investigated.
Jan. 6-7, 2021: voted against certifying the 2020 presidential election results and voted against the second Trump impeachment (Jan. 13, 2021).
During COVID-19 he argued the FDA 'deep state' was blocking hydroxychloroquine; medical experts (Mayo Clinic, cited on Wikipedia) say it neither treats nor prevents COVID-19.

endorsements.text: Donald Trump (Oct. 2025); AIPAC; Associated Builders and Contractors Florida Gulf Coast Chapter (per Wikipedia).

owner_sources.title: FEMA Official's Directive to Ignore Homes With Trump Flags Not 'Isolated Incident' - Came From Top of FEMA, Says GOP Rep
owner_sources.says: Per the search excerpt only (page returned 403): Steube claims a FEMA directive to skip homes with Trump signs after Hurricane Helene was systemic, not a one-off. His allegation, not an established finding; not fact-checked.

votes.what: Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.
Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.
Federal Immigration Enforcement ('Rule of Law Adherence Act'): requires state and local agencies to comply with federal immigration law and bars sanctuary-type restrictions.
Self-defense immunity: puts the burden of proof on prosecutors when a defendant claims Stand Your Ground immunity.
Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School Public Safety Act: raised the age to buy long guns to 21, created waiting period, school marshal/guardian program, funding for school safety.
